questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8001: A $3,450 bond issued at a discount pays $14,250 of cash interest this period and has $550 of discount amortization. What is interest expense?

options.misconception: uses only cash interest and ignores the discount amortization
subtracts discount amortization from cash interest
uses the coupon on face value rather than effective expense

questions.explanation: When bonds are issued at a discount, interest expense exceeds the cash paid because the discount amortization is an additional financing cost, so $14,250 plus $550 gives $14,800. Subtracting the amortization would describe a premium bond instead.
questions.hint: A discount increases interest expense above the cash paid.

provenance.author: bank-team-acct
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.learningObjective: Compute interest expense on discount bonds

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8002: Clearwater Works has 69 shares of 6 percent preferred stock with a $14 par value. What is the annual preferred dividend?

options.misconception: computes the dividend on one share rather than all shares
uses total par value and ignores the dividend rate
uses sixty percent instead of six percent

questions.explanation: Preferred dividends equal shares times par value times the stated rate, so 69 shares times $14 times six percent is $58. Applying the rate to only one share or omitting it entirely would misstate the annual obligation.
questions.hint: Multiply shares by par value by the dividend percentage.

questions.stem: Case 8003: Foxglove Supply has total stockholders' equity of $2,750, including $750 of preferred stock, and 30 shares of common stock outstanding. What is book value per common share?

includes preferred stock in the common shareholders' claim
reports total common equity rather than a per-share amount

questions.explanation: Book value per common share divides the equity attributable to common shareholders by shares outstanding, so $2,750 less $750 divided by 30 gives $67. Preferred stock must be deducted because it belongs to a different class of owners.
questions.hint: Remove preferred equity before dividing by common shares.

questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 8004: On November 12, 2025, the board of Hawthorne Traders declares a $2,400 cash dividend to be paid later. Which entry records the declaration?

options.misconception: reverses the debit and credit sides of the entry
debits the wrong account while leaving the credit unchanged
credits the wrong account while leaving the debit unchanged

questions.explanation: Declaration creates an obligation, so Dividends is debited for $2,400 and Dividends Payable is credited. Cash is not credited at declaration because no payment has occurred yet; the cash entry is made on the payment date.
